subject: Azure private offer: commit smoothing and channel margin allocation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@aurora-tech.com>, procure@aurora-tech.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Azure private offer: commit smoothing and channel margin allocation

Hi Elena / procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Following up with a proposed structure for the Azure private offer so we can align on pricing cadence and channel passback:

- Commit smoothing: propose we anchor billing to a 3-month committed consumption profile with a 70/20/10 smoothing (month 1/2/3) to reduce month-to-month spikes for Aurora. We can convert any under-consumption into a one-time credit or roll it into month 4 as long as total annual committed units are met.
- Channel margin allocation: Redwood recommends a two-tier waterfall: 18% reseller passback on committed usage up to the committed threshold, then 10% on overage consumed beyond the threshold. One-time professional services should be excluded from the passback.
- Billing mechanics: commit will be invoiced monthly at the smoothed rate; overages billed monthly with a 30-day reconciliation.

I've attached a preliminary pricing workbook to illustrate net vs list price and the proposed waterfall (Aurora_prelim_pricing.xlsx). Ben and Connor are looped in to confirm margin feasibility from our side.

Questions for you:
1) Does Aurora have a procurement preference for smoothing percentages (e.g., 50/30/20, 80/20/0, etc.)?
2) Any constraints on reseller passback being accounted as credits vs direct invoice reductions?
3) Would Aurora need usage visibility at the SKU level or is aggregated consumption OK for reconciliation?

If helpful I can set a 30-min sync tomorrow to go through the workbook and trade-offs.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Mountain Region
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@aurora-tech.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer: commit smoothing and channel margin allocation

Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up and the workbook. Quick answers and constraints from Aurora's procurement side:

- We prefer a fairly front-loaded smoothing (80/20/0) for quarterly commitments to keep Q1 predictable for our finance team. That said, we can entertain 70/20/10 if it simplifies quoting on your end.
- Reseller passback: Aurora needs passback recorded as a credit on our monthly invoice rather than as a separate payment. Our AP team cannot process negative invoices easily, so credits are preferable.
- Usage granularity: aggregated consumption by product family is fine for reconciliation; SKU-level would be nice-to-have but not required at first.

Procurement attached a short constraints doc and a sample commitment spreadsheet so you can map it to your waterfall (Aurora_prelim_pricing.xlsx).

Two specific asks:
1) Can you confirm whether your 18% reseller passback is calculated on net-of-discount list price or gross list price?
2) Any flexibility to treat the first 3 months of commit as refundable credits if Aurora under-delivers >20% of the quarter?

We'd like to align before we send to legal. Available for a quick call tomorrow afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Cloud Procurement
Aurora Tech
elena.ruiz@aurora-tech.com
Attachment: Aurora_prelim_pricing.xlsx (procurement constraints, 2 pages)

Elena / team — looping in the margin ops view and a concrete waterfall so procurement can see the math.

Key points:
- Passback base: Redwood calculates reseller passback off the customer-facing net invoice (post any platform discounts, pre-tax). That makes credits straightforward to apply on your invoice.
- Margin waterfall (attached):
  * Tier 1: up to commit (anchored 3-month smoothed amount) — 18% credit applied monthly
  * Tier 2: 100-125% of commit — 12% credit on incremental usage
  * Tier 3: >125% — 8% credit on incremental usage
- Refundable credits: we can provide a limited refundable credit for under-delivery only if Aurora commits to minimum annual consumption and signs a short amendment that specifies the credit mechanism. Otherwise we roll under-consumption into future month(s) or issue a one-time invoice credit at quarter close.
- Professional services and one-time setup fees excluded from credit calculations.

I've attached a worked example in Redwood_margin_waterfall_v1.xlsx — shows a sample commit, smoothing variants (80/20/0 vs 70/20/10), and net economics to Aurora and the reseller.

Propose a 30-min call on Tue 1:30pm PT to walk the workbook and decide smoothing. Naomi — can you send a calendar invite?

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick summary and agreed next steps so legal/procurement have a clean handoff:

Decisions:
- Smoothing: Aurora prefers 80/20/0 quarterly smoothing. Redwood will price using that profile for the initial quote.
- Passback mechanics: Redwood will apply reseller credits on the monthly invoice (net-of-platform-discounts) as Elena requested.
- Waterfall: locked to the tiers Ben outlined (18% up to commit, 12% 100-125%, 8% >125%).
- Under-delivery: if quarterly consumption is >20% below the smoothed commit, Redwood will issue a one-time invoice credit unless Aurora signs the annual minimum amendment (we will include language in the commercial worksheet).

Action items:
- Naomi: update the pricing workbook to reflect 80/20/0 smoothing and export a commercial worksheet for Aurora legal (attached: MAP_v1.pdf). Due EOD Wed.
- Ben: finalize the margin waterfall tab and confirm passback calculation column headers for Aurora AP. Due EOD Wed.
- Aurora procurement: confirm whether invoice credit language is acceptable or if you require refundable credits in writing.
- If everyone agrees, Naomi to send a calendar invite for Wed 10am PT to finalize before legal review.
